# dsh-token-usage-heatmap

A token usage panel for the DSH Web GUI. It folds the session logs already on
disk into per-day buck

ets and draws them as a 26-week heatmap, a per-model bar
chart and a compact total in the header.

Nothing leaves the machine: the roll-up is computed by the host from local
session logs and served o
nly to this machine's own loopback GUI.
## What it shows
**Overview tab**

- A 26-week calendar heatmap of daily token usage, one cell per day, four blue
levels scaled to the

busiest day in the current range. Cells are week-aligned:
the grid is always 26 columns and only adv

ances on Sundays, so it does not
shift under the pointer as days pass.
- Six figures for the selecte

d range: total tokens, messages, sessions, active
days, peak hour, and most-used model.
- A "your us

age is worth N copies of …" line comparing the total against the
token count of well-known books.
**Models tab**

- A stacked daily bar chart plus a per-model ranking with session counts.
- The axis keeps exactly t

hree ticks (0, half, peak) at every usage level, and
the top tick is rounded *up* so a bar can never

(0, half, peak) at every usage level, and
the top tick is rounded *up* so a bar can never cross it.

**Ranges** — 全部 / 30 天 / 7 天. "全部" means every day on disk, not the 26
weeks the grid happens to dra

w. The bar chart uses a 30-day window for 全部 and
30 天, and a 7-day window for 7 天.

**Header chip** — a compact token total at the left of the session header. It
polls once a minute, r

efreshes on window focus, and retries briefly on a cold
start, so it does not stay frozen on the val
ue it saw when the page loaded.

**Click-to-open panel** — the chip is the button. Clicking it drops the full
panel below it as a flo

ating card; the same click, the panel's × button, a
click outside, or Escape closes it again. The ca

rd is rendered through a React
portal on `document.body`, so it is never squeezed by the composer's

flex
layout, and on a short window only the card's own body scrolls. Its open state
is remembered be

d on a short window only the card's own body scrolls. Its open state
is remembered between sessions.
## Theme support

Light and dark palettes are separate sets of opaque colours. The dark set is not
the light set at lo

w opacity: a translucent step over the dark card surface reads
as a black square, so each level carr
ies an explicit colour in both themes.
## Settings
The plugin adds three switches under **Settings → General**:
| Switch | Effect |
| Show the usage chip in the header | Hides the header chip, and with it the panel's only entry poin

t |
| Open the panel from the chip on a new session | When off, the new-session chip shows the total

but opens nothing |
| Open the panel from the chip inside a conversation | When off, the in-convers
ation chip shows the total but opens nothing |

The switches are stored in the Host configuration, so they apply to every
window of this profile.
## Install
Through the app: **Settings → Plugins**, then install `dsh-token-usage-heatmap`.
From GitHub, against a named profile:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
From this folder before it is published:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Restart the host after installing; a newly loaded JavaScript bundle needs it.
For DSH Desktop the pr

ofile is managed by the app, so use **Settings → Plugins**
there rather than the command line.
## How it works

- `lib/fold.js` reads session logs under `$DSH_HOME/sessions`, both plain
`session*.jsonl` and multi

-frame `session*.jsonl.zstd`, and folds each one into
per-day, per-hour and per-model buckets.
- `li

b/usage.js` merges the sessions into a roll-up and caches it at
`$DSH_HOME/cache/token-usage-heatmap

/usage.<pid>.json`, so a warm start does
not re-read every log.
- `lib/index.js` registers one exact

route, `/token-usage-heatmap/usage`, which
answers JSON. It requires a loopback `Host` header, refu

ses
`sec-fetch-site: cross-site`, and requires any `Origin` to match the host — a
web page elsewhere

must not be able to read your whole token history.
- `lib/client.js` is the browser half: one entry

in
`conversation.header.leading` that renders both the chip and the panel, plus
the switches in `se

ttings.general.item`. The panel is a popper portalled to
`document.body`, so it is positioned under

the chip and never squeezed by the
composer's flex layout; click the chip, its × button, or press Es

cape to
close it. The `conversation.input.dock` slot is intentionally unused.

The plugin declares `dsh.bundle` with `cordis.patch.yml`, so it installs as a
bundle and its row can
be switched on and off like any other plugin.
## Requirements

- A DSH host that serves the Web GUI and exposes `webServer` to plugins.
- Node 22.15 or newer, or a

ny runtime whose `node:zlib` exports
`zstdDecompressSync`. On an older runtime the plugin still load

s and serves
the route; only compressed session logs (`.jsonl.zstd`) are skipped, so plain
`.jsonl`

logs still count.
- No build step and no dependencies: the published package is plain JavaScript.
